query: Are the four packages the deep-research-agent pipeline depends on — pi-web-access, pi-subagents, @zhushanwen/pi-structured-output, pi-workflow-engine — actively maintained, and do their current published versions still provide the capabilities the pipeline's stage contracts assume?
scope_constraints: Current published state as of the run date; installed local copies (pi-web-access 0.27.0, pi-subagents 0.79.1, pi-workflow-engine 1.1.0, @zhushanwen/pi-structured-output 6.2.1) are the baseline for comparison, not the evidence

Primary sources only: official package registry pages, package repositories (github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access, github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents, github.com/timbrinded/pi-workflow-engine), and package docs; a repository URL for @zhushanwen/pi-structured-output must be found, not assumed
The capability baseline being checked is what stages/01_plan–04_report and _shared/infrastructure.md assume

research_questions.question: What is the current published version of each of the four packages, and when was it published?
success_criteria: Current version number and publish date per package, from the official registry page for each of the four packages
Installed-vs-current version delta recorded per package

research_questions.question: Does the current published version of each package still expose the specific capabilities the stage contracts assume?
success_criteria: pi-web-access: current docs/source confirm web_search, fetch_content, source_check, get_search_content are registered tools
pi-subagents: current docs/source confirm the researcher and evidence-auditor agent definitions ship, with foreground/background delegation
@zhushanwen/pi-structured-output: current docs/source confirm Ajv-backed validation and an authoritative-schema injection mode usable as a trust boundary
pi-workflow-engine: current docs/source confirm the workflow tool with gates, budgets, and structured-output contracts
Each capability finding names the page or file that establishes it

research_questions.question: Is each package actively maintained — recent release or commit activity, and no deprecation or archival notices?
success_criteria: Last release or commit date per package, from its repository or registry page
Deprecation, archival, or unmaintained flags explicitly checked and their absence or presence recorded per package

research_questions.question: Where the current published version differs from the installed one, do the release notes describe changes that would break the pipeline's assumptions?
success_criteria: Release notes or changelog read for every package whose current version differs from the installed baseline
Any breaking change that affects an assumed capability is named with its version and the capability it touches

queries: pi-web-access current documentation: registered tools web_search fetch_content source_check get_search_content
pi-subagents current documentation: researcher and evidence-auditor agent definitions, delegation modes
@zhushanwen/pi-structured-output current documentation: Ajv validation, authoritative schema injection
pi-workflow-engine current documentation: workflow tool gates budgets structured-output contracts
Commit and release activity per package repository — via the repository links surfaced by RQ1's registry pages and RQ2's documentation; check deprecation notices on those same pages

Release notes / changelogs between the installed baseline versions and the current published versions — via the repository changelogs surfaced by RQ1–RQ3, read only for the packages where a version gap exists

required_evidence: Official registry page per package showing current version and publish date
Package documentation or source establishing each capability named in the stage contracts and _shared/infrastructure.md
Repository activity evidence (last release or commit) per package
Release notes or changelog entries for every installed-to-current version gap
